page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds is an x86_64 compute instance powered by an Intel processor and hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine features 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 84.0 GB of system memory, delivering an exceptionally high memory allocation of 21.0 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

Local storage is provided as a bundled 180 GB solid-state drive (SSD), and the configuration supports integration with Azure Premium Storage for persistent high-throughput disk workloads. Network routing requires customer-managed allocation, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The architectural design prioritizes memory density over multi-threaded core volume. Because no benchmark metrics are recorded for this instance type, its operational baseline is defined by its hardware ratio. This resource profile offers cost efficiency for applications that are bound by memory capacity rather than core scaling, allowing organizations to avoid licensing and running surplus vCPUs simply to obtain adequate RAM. The instance fits in-memory caching platforms, memory-intensive database engines, data transformation pipelines, and enterprise application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure FX4mds is a memory-dense virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs on an Intel processor platform under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Designed around an asymmetric compute-to-memory configuration, the instance delivers 84.0 GB of RAM, equating to 21.0 GB per vCPU, without hardware GPU acceleration. Storage capabilities include a bundled 180 GB local SSD along with support for Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This infrastructure balance provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-constrained environments, removing the requirement to provision higher core-count instances solely to satisfy working memory requirements. The FX4mds is suited for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, caching systems, analytics processing, and mid-sized transactional application servers.
